title: Flatness of degree-zero opcycles of a bounded-above free model
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $d$ a natural number, and $C^\bullet,Q^\bullet$ cochain complexes of structure-sheaf modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Assume $C^n=0$ for $n<0$ and $n>d$, $Q^n=0$ for $n>d$, each $C^n$ is flat over the identity of $X$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], and for every integer $n$ there is a natural number $r_n$ and an isomorphism $Q^n\cong\mathcal O_X^{r_n}$. Let $e:Q^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Then the actual cokernel $Q^0/\operatorname{im}(Q^{-1}\to Q^0)$ is flat over the identity of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0653, label lemma-last-one-flat, applied at every stalk; affine localization comparisons are Tags 01U4 and 00HT. Source text checked on the Stacks website; the local source checkout is absent.

proof.text: Fix x and an affine neighbourhood V with coordinate ring A. Affine neighbourhoods W of x contained in V are cofinal among neighbourhoods. IsFlatOver for each C term gives flatness of its sections on every such W over A. Express the stalk as their filtered colimit; filtered-colimit flatness gives flatness over A. The stalk ring is the localization of A at the prime of x, so flatness over A is equivalent to flatness over this stalk ring. Q has finite free stalks. Both complexes retain their upper bound, and C retains its nonnegative lower bound.

The exact stalk functor carries e to a quasi-isomorphism of module complexes. Both bounded-above flat stalk complexes are K-flat. A quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes stays a quasi-isomorphism after tensoring with any module N in degree zero. Its target is concentrated in nonnegative degrees, so the source tensor complex is exact in degree -1. The module formulation of the tensor comparison is the one-point-site formulation, transported through the equivalence with modules.

Apply the flat-opcycles Tor criterion to the stalk complex of Q at a=0. Its terms are free, hence flat, and tensor exactness in degree -1 was just established. Stalks preserve the cokernel, so the conclusion is flatness of the stalk of Q.opcycles(0).

The cokernel of Q^(-1) to Q^0 has a finite free presentation, hence is quasi-coherent. On any affine V the stalks are the localizations of its section module by the affine section/stalk tensor identification. The module local flatness criterion gives flatness of sections on V. For affine W contained in V, the section module on W is flat over its own coordinate ring, and that ring is flat over the ring of V since the inclusion is an open immersion. Transitivity gives exactly IsFlatOver for the identity. The zero module and the empty scheme need no nontriviality hypothesis.

theorem isFlatOver_opcycles_zero_of_quasiIso {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (C Q : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ) (d : ℕ)
    (hCge : C.IsStrictlyGE 0) (hCle : C.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (hCflat : ∀ n : ℤ, (C.X n).IsFlatOver (𝟙 X))
    (hQle : Q.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (hQfree : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ,
      Nonempty (Q.X n ≅ SheafOfModules.free
        (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
    (e : Q ⟶ C) (he : QuasiIso e) :
    (Q.opcycles 0).IsFlatOver (𝟙 X)
